full_judgment: 5. The plaintiff preferred an appeal against the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge, which being heard by the Court of the Additional District Judge, Chittagong was allowed and the suit was decreed declaring the plaintiff's title to the disputed land and also decreeing recovery for Khas possession of the disputed land by evicting defendant No. 2 and 3 therefrom. In course of the Judgment, the learned Additional District Judge came to the findings that the story of tenancy in respect of the disputed land since 1940 as set up by defendant Nos. 2 and 3 was a mere concoction that there was no contract to sell in favour of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 in respect of the disputed land in 1949 nor any earnest money was paid in pursuance of the said contract, that the contesting defendants had been in possession of the disputed land since 1956-57 and that the suit being filed in 1961, mere was no acquisition of valid title by adverse possession. As regards the legal effect of the lease Ext. C and the kabala, Ext. D the learned Additional District Judge appears to be of the view, concurrently with the learned Subordinate Judge, that the deed of lease Ext C was void in view of section 9 and section 75A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the kabala, Ext. D, by which the rent-receiving interest was purported to have been transferred was also void in inasmuch as no private person could sell the rent-receiving-interest after the 14th April, 1956.
